title: ac edit and at edit assert behavioural guarantees in help that 0142's detector cannot see, so the unguarded population is at least 6 not 4
body:
`ac edit` and `at edit` shipped behavioural guarantees in their help strings that 0142's detector cannot see by construction, so the unguarded-help-string population is at least 6, not 4.

MEASURED by ic 2026-08-29 against the delivered pair `30a2dd81`.

## The population claim in 0142 is a floor, and these are two more members

0142 records: "POPULATION: 4 OF 118 SHIPPED ROWS assert a precondition or refusal in `help`", with `at green` FALSE and `ac new` / `at new` TRUE. It also states, correctly, that the 4 is a floor because the detector is "a regex over English -- only from, refuses, requires, must, cannot, unless".

`ac edit` and `at edit` landed in `8aebe2ce` -- the SAME commit that fixed two of the original four -- and both assert a behavioural guarantee in help:

    ac edit :: Reword a criterion, leaving its kind and its satisfaction alone
    at edit :: Re-cite an acceptance test; a field you do not name is a field it does not change

Neither sentence contains any of the six detector words. They are invisible to it not by accident but by construction, which is exactly the floor 0142 predicted.

## Both are TRUE today, driven, and that is the point rather than a reprieve

- `ac edit --text` on a satisfied criterion: `satisfied: yes` before and after. The guarantee holds.
- `at edit --covers` with an unchanged value: `ok: AT-01.1 already unchanged`, rc=0, nothing moved. The guarantee holds, and the no-op message is honest.

True-and-unguarded is the position `at green` occupied before its behaviour drifted away from its help string. Nothing checks either sentence and nothing updates it when the behaviour moves.

## The caveat is placed where the answer is known and absent where it is not

`docs/reference/intent-ac.md:331` and `docs/reference/intent-at.md:230` carry the 0142 caveat -- "treat this line as a description, not a guarantee" -- over `ac new` and `at new`. Both of those have now been driven independently of their builder and both refusals are TRUE (rc=1, nothing written, remedy naming the sibling edit verb).

`ac edit` and `at edit` carry no caveat at all.

So the warning currently sits on the two rows whose guarantees are verified and is missing from the two that nobody has checked. A correct general warning, applied where the specific answer is known, destroys information; its absence where the answer is unknown withholds it. Both halves are wrong in the same direction.

## What this is NOT

Not a request to widen the detector's regex. 0142 already rules that a prose-regex gate for a population of this size is the ST0039 greppable-proxy shape -- a mechanical check standing in for a judgement it cannot make -- and that reasoning is unchanged by these two members. The finding is that the POPULATION is bigger than recorded and that the two newest members arrived unmarked in the commit that fixed two of the old ones.

## Bearing on 0142's structural half

This is the same gap from the other side: refusals and behavioural guarantees have no structural home in the register, so the only place to state one is a help string. Two more verbs have now shipped into that position. Any new verb that asserts a guarantee joins it silently, which is what makes the structural half worth building rather than re-counting the population each time.
